note: Bored-investor critique of the Anchor Re-architecture implementation plan.

findings.section: Wave 17 — W17 — C4 Live Demo + ConPTY Verdict Application
findings.message: The plan leaves the YES branch of the ConPTY spike unresolved; if the spike succeeds, there is no defined wave in this plan to implement the actual ConPTY integration, making the plan incomplete for the successful spike outcome.

findings.section: Wave 16 — W16 — External Supervisor Service + Live Probes
findings.message: While the plan asserts that spawned jobs survive a supervisor restart via breakaway, it lacks any mechanism for the restarted supervisor to locate, re-identify, and rebuild its internal job-to-PID tracking map to resume management of those orphaned processes.

findings.section: Wave 9 — W9 — Auth Enforce + Cookie Navigation + Ops Cutover (C2 gate)
findings.criterion: One route table, declarative auth, default-deny.
findings.message: The plan mandates cookie-based navigation for the gated data plane but fails to define how the auth cookie is initially requested, generated, and set on the client (e.g., via a login endpoint or bootstrap handshake) when ANCHOR_TOKEN is active.

findings.section: Wave 6 — W6 — Extraction Increment 3: generate_html JS/CSS → static (C1 exit gate)
findings.message: The static CSS/JS extraction does not modernize the dashboard's visual theme or layout using Tailwind CSS, keeping the legacy aesthetic intact.
